instruction: Vision signal: 49% fall armyworm, 42% African armyworm. Farmer: My maize whorl is chewed. Which pest is it?
response: The signal is too close to name the pest confidently. Is the damage concentrated in the whorl with fresh, moist frass, and can you describe the caterpillar's head and body markings? Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: I found an egg mass on a maize leaf. How do I tell if it is fall armyworm?
response: Check whether the eggs are laid in a mass covered with hairs or scales, and note where on the plant they sit. If you are not sure, do not force an identification. Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: I saw an adult moth near my field. Does that mean the whole field is infested?
response: No. A moth means FAW is present in the area, but not that every plant has live larvae. Scout your plants for fresh feeding damage before acting. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction:
How should I scout my maize for FAW?<end_of_turn>
<start_of_turn>model
Walk the field in a W pattern and inspect stations of 10 plants.<end_of_turn>
<start_of_turn>user
What exactly counts as a plant that is currently infested?
response: Count a plant as currently infested only when it shows fresh whorl damage or fresh frass, not old holes alone. Record those plants to judge the current infestation level. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Alamar hoton gona: 47% kwaron soja, 44% cutworm. Manomi: Ana yanke tsire-tsire na kusa da ƙasa. Menene?
response: Alamar ba ta da ƙarfi don in tabbatar. Shin ana yanke shuke-shuke kusa da ƙasa, ko kuwa kana ganin sabuwar barna a cikin ramin masara? Za ka iya bayyana yadda tsutsar take idan ka same ta? Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: Ta yaya zan tabbatar da kwaron soja idan na kama tsutsa?
response: Nemi alamar Y mai juyewa a gaban baƙar kai da ɗigo huɗu masu duhu da suka yi kama da murabba'i kusa da ƙarshen jiki. Waɗannan alamun jiki ne mafi tabbaci. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Wadanne sabbin alamu a ramin masara ke nuna kwaron soja yana ci a yanzu?
response: Sabbin ramukan cizo da sabon bayan gari (frass) mai laima a cikin ramin masara na nuna cewa tsutsa tana ci a yanzu, ba tsoffin ramuka ba. Source: FAO, FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction:
Zan iya amfani da wani maganin kwari saboda kwaron soja ya dawo?<end_of_turn>
<start_of_turn>model
Ka tabbatar an yi wa samfurin rajista don amfanin gona da kwaron a yankinka.<end_of_turn>
<start_of_turn>user
Nawa zan yi amfani da shi?
response: Ban ba da adadin magani ba. Ka bi umarnin lakabin samfurin da aka yi wa rajista game da adadi, kariya da lokacin girbi. Kada ka yi kiyasin adadi daga wani samfuri. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Vision signal: 53% fall armyworm, 38% stem borer. Farmer: Enwere m oghere n'akwụkwọ ọka m. Kedu ihe ọ bụ?
response: Signal ahụ esighị ike iji kpọọ ya n'aka. Oghere ndị ahụ ọ dị n'ime olulu ọka na frass ọhụrụ? Ị nwere ike ịkọwa akara dị n'isi na ahụ larva ma ọ bụrụ na ị hụrụ ya? Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Ahụrụ m egg mass n'akwụkwọ ọka. Kedu ka m ga-esi mata ma ọ bụ FAW?
response: Lelee ma eggs ahụ dị ka otu mass ma nwee ntutu ma ọ bụ scales n'elu, ma mara ebe ha dị n'osisi ahụ. Ọ bụrụ na ị maghị, ajụla ịkọ na ọ bụ FAW. Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Intercropping ọka na soybean nwere ike ibelata FAW?
response: Crop diversification nwere ike ibelata nrụgide FAW n'ụfọdụ usoro ugbo. Nnyocha Naịjirịa 2025 hụrụ obere FAW incidence na damage n'ọka a gwakọtara na soybean karịa naanị ọka. Were ya dị ka ihe akaebe mpaghara, ọ bụghị nkwa maka ubi ọ bụla. Source: Jibril & Ahmed (2025), AGRIS.

instruction: Kedu ihe na-egosi na fall armyworm nọ na-eri ọka m ugbu a?
response: Oghere ọhụrụ na frass ọhụrụ n'ime olulu ọka na-egosi na larva na-eri nri ugbu a. Lelee olulu, ọ bụghị naanị oghere ochie. Source: FAO, FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Báwo ni mo ṣe lè dá ọ̀gbìn ológun mọ̀ yàtọ̀ sí ìdin míì tí mo bá rí i?
response: Wá àmì Y tí ó yí padà lórí iwájú orí dúdú àti àmì mẹ́rin dúdú tí wọ́n ṣe onígun mẹ́rin lórí apá ara tó sún mọ́ ìkẹyìn. Àwọn àmì ara wọ̀nyí ni ó dájú jù. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Àmì tuntun wo nínú ihò àgbàdo ló ń fi hàn pé ọ̀gbìn ológun ń jẹ ẹ́ lọ́wọ́?
response: Àwọn ihò ìjẹ tuntun àti frass tuntun nínú ihò àgbàdo ń fi hàn pé ìdin ń jẹun lọ́wọ́, kì í ṣe àwọn ihò àtijọ́. Source: FAO, FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Ṣé rírí moth àgbà kan túmọ̀ sí pé gbogbo oko mi ti ní ìdin?
response: Rárá. Moth ń fi hàn pé FAW wà ní agbègbè, ṣùgbọ́n kò fi hàn pé gbogbo ewéko ní ìdin alààyè. Ṣàyẹ̀wò àwọn ewéko fún ìbàjẹ́ tuntun kí o tó gbé ìgbésẹ̀. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Mo rí egg mass lórí ewé àgbàdo. Ṣé ọ̀gbìn ológun ni?
response: Mi ò lè dájú láti inú èyí nìkan. Ṣé egg mass náà ní irun tàbí scales lórí rẹ̀, àti níbo ni ó wà lórí ewéko náà? Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Vision signal: 46% fall armyworm, 45% cutworm. Farmer: Something dey cut my seedlings near the ground. Which one be this?
response: The signal too close to confirm. The plants dey cut near the ground, or you dey see fresh damage inside the whorl? If you fit find the caterpillar, describe how e take look. Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: How I fit confirm say na fall armyworm when I catch the caterpillar?
response: Look for the pale upside-down Y for the front of the dark head, and four dark spots wey arrange like square near the last body segment. These body marks na the surest sign. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: How I go take scout my maize field for FAW?
response: Waka the field for W pattern. For the start, every turn, and the end, check 10 plants in a row for fresh whorl damage or fresh frass, then record only the plants wey get current signs. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: I see FAW eggs and small caterpillars for my farm. Wetin I fit do?
response: Where e practical, remove and destroy the egg masses and young larvae wey you find. Early manual action na part of FAO integrated approach. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).
